OVERDUE JUSTICE FOR CHILD ABUSE

By: Ntokozo Miya | Paid

Proposal


Show: Carte Blanche

One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...):
It took 40 years for these victims to find the courage to expose their abusers and now that they have named and shamed the culprits, the women will stop at nothing to get justice.

Unique Selling Point:
Not only do we speak to Alex and Claudine about their abuse, but we also speak to Suzanne, a victim who has never been interviewed before. We also tell a visually compelling story that incorporates a Cape Talk interview.


Summary:
Victims of an alleged pedophile speak out more that 40 years after the abuse happened. Alex Bowles and her brother John were abused by family friend John Hardwick. Alex talks us through the years of abuse as well as how the adults in their circle, including their parents, enabled it to happen. Alex talks about how her trauma and how that manifested in drug and alcohol addiction as well as eating disorders. She discusses her struggles with nurturing meaningful relationships over the years. She explains the motivation for the R15 million lawsuit against the now 82-year old Hardwick.

We also interview Claudine Shiels who also took her abuser to court more than 40 years after the abuse. She took the matter to court in 2017 and will unpack the events of the legal journey in the years that followed, highlighting her wins and losses.

Experts provide context for the topic – Zoom interview conducted by Cape Talk with Ian Levit, the lawyer for Alex and an interview with a psychiatrist who discusses grooming behaviour of pedophiles, how enablers create the perfect environment for abuse and how related trauma affects victims.

Further information:
More than anything, in a society where many victims carry the weight of the abuse secret for their whole lives, until they take it to their grave – we put the spotlight on those who have found the courage to speak out and turn to the courts for justice, even after so much time has passed.


Extra Budget Items:
Same-day, return flights for presenter and producer - depart for Cape Town in the morning, return to Johannesburg in the evening.

Press Release:


The Reckoning
Justice can be difficult to come by for the adult survivors of childhood sexual abuse. But one woman's quest to reckon with the past has revealed more victims and, together, they are facing off against the 80-year-old man they say molested them. In 2018, the Constitutional Court ruled these crimes can be prosecuted, no matter how long ago the abuse took place. Now, some remarkable adults are demanding a price for a childhood tainted by suffering. In collaboration with Primedia’s 567 Cape Talk, Carte Blanche meets three courageous women out for justice decades after suffering the abuse.
Producer: Ntokozo Sindane | Presenter: Claire Mawisa

Script:


APPROVED FINAL MIX - HISTORIC CHILD ABUSE
AUDIO
VO – Home: a place of safety and comfort. A place of love, too, shared with protective parents. That, at least, is how things should be.
But that’s not what home meant to these two women - strangers meeting for the first time, but with stories that bind them together.
CAPE TALK BUMPER – RADIO SHOW PART ONE

Join the conversation, you're with Cape Talk...
PIPPA HUDSON - CAPE TALK

Alex Bowles is with me in studio. She recently took the decision that she would no longer stay silent about the abuse that she endured as a child.
VO - Alex Bowles and Claudine Shiels are both survivors of childhood sexual abuse, bravely telling their stories years later.
Alex, who grew up in a leafy Johannesburg suburb, says she was sexually assaulted by a family friend.
ALEX BOWLES – ABUSE SURVIVOR

I have kept this secret for all these years. He's been able to wander through our lives causing destruction.
VO – Claudine's childhood in the Eastern Cape was also scarred by abuse. Both she and her sister fell victim to two men close to their family.
CLAUDINE SHIELS – ABUSE SURVIVOR

It steals so much from you. It takes so much from you. It changes your entire life.
LINK – Anger, guilt, shame – these are the feelings that plague the victims of historic child abuse that cause them to suffer in silence. But decades later, some survivors are not only choosing to expose the attocities committed against them, they are demanding justice.
VO – Much of Alex's childhood in Johannesburg was spent in a tight knit circle with her family and their friends.
ALEX BOWLES – ABUSE SURVIVOR

Believe you me, we had huge braais, if not every weekend, most weekends.
VO – The alleged abuser was always the life of the party - a favorite uncle amongst the children.
ALEX BOWLES – ABUSE SURVIVOR

He'd have his camera slung over the shoulder and he was just always there. He used to say to me: “I think you could be Miss South Africa one day, let's go take some photos.”
VO - A sinister ruse to spend time alone with 10-year old Alex.
ALEX BOWLES – ABUSE SURVIVOR

…and then the hand would move to the boob. He put his hand in my pants and up my vagina.
VO - Now Alex wants her abuser to account. Her alleged perpetrator – who can legally be named – is this man, John Hardwick.
ALEX BOWLES – ABUSE SURVIVOR

John Hardwick was in our lives from the year dot and that really bothers me because I don't know when it all started.
VO – Forensic psychiatrist Dr Giada Del Fabbro has dealt extensively with historic child abuse cases.
DR GIADA DEL FABBRO – FORENSIC PSYCHIATRIST – CLIP0059

They will manipulate the child into believing that what they will do with the perpetrator is normal, an expression of love.
VO – In 1985, Alex learned of another – unexpected - victim.
ALEX BOWLES – ABUSE SURVIVOR

My brother was on his way to boarding school at KES and my mum did the talk. You know, boys might try and do this. And my brother said, Oh, you mean like Uncle John?
VO – Shockingly, their parents didn’t act, and Uncle John continued to be invited into their home.

Three years after her brother’s admission, Alex told her parents that their friend had also been abusing her.
ALEX BOWLES – ABUSE SURVIVOR

My father said to him, if you get help, go for counseling, you can stay in our family circle, you know, of friends. If not, we're going to cut ties.
VO – But the ties remained intact.
LINK – Predators don't reserve their grooming tactics exclusively for their targets, parents are also drawn in with a toxic serenade that allows the predators easy access to the children that they intend to abuse.
VO – Hardwick's friendship with Alex's parents began a few years before she was born.
ALEX BOWLES – ABUSE SURVIVOR

In 1966, my father was offered a job by his father in law.
VO – Alex’s parents initially denied knowing that Hardwick was a predator, but when confronted with an incident at a dinner party in the seventies, her own father defended Hardwick’s actions.
ALEX BOWLES – ABUSE SURVIVOR

ALEX - There was a little girl of six there. She says that man tried to put his hands in my pants. Her father got up once he heard and he broke John Hardwick's nose. My father wanted the father arrested for assault, not John Hardwick for child abuse.

CLAIRE - Was it the ultimate betrayal by your parents, do you feel?

ALEX – Yes. For me, enablers of this sort of crime also have blood on their hands.
VO: Years later, Alex and her brother cut all ties with their parents.
DR GIADA DEL FABBRO – FORENSIC PSYCHIATRIST – CLIP0062

CLAIRE – Why is it that some sexual abuse victims take years to eventually speak out?

DR DEL FABBRO – They feel like they were responsible for it in some way. It is very difficult for them to speak out because they fear being blamed, being shamed, being told it was their fault.
VO - Daunting as speaking out may be, taking things a step further is arguably even more difficult, as Claudine knows all too well. She and her sister have been seeking justice against the men who assaulted them for several years.
CLAUDINE SHIELS – ABUSE SURVIVOR

CLAUDINE - It's now 48 years, that's the age of our case and we have now passed the 4 year mark since we laid charges and we don't even have a sniff of a trial date ahead of us,

PIPPA – It's been 4 years, has it been worth it?

CLAUDINE – Absolutely and I won’t give up. I spent years in therapy. My life did not turn out the way I wanted it to turn out and so, I have to be part of this fight back.
VO – Claudine details the abuse in her book 'Walking Through Front Doors'.
CLAUDINE SHIELS – ABUSE SURVIVOR

CLAUDINE – My sister and I were abused by two men who had access to us and who stayed at our house fairly often.

CLAIRE - What do you envision as justice in your particular case?

CLAUDINE - Just to be able to tell our story, to be heard, to have so many people take us seriously and to have the law take us seriously.
VO – For her sanity, Claudine does not let the case consume her.
CLAUDINE SHIELS – ABUSE SURVIVOR

I write, I'm back at university studying, you know, that's also how I've dealt with the discouragement and the long and tedious road that we that we're walking.
VO - But, if you think the prospect of walking her own long and tedious road might discourage Alex, well, you couldn’t be more wrong. She has far too many painful reminders of her past to simply let it go.
ALEX BOWLES – ABUSE SURVIVOR

The seductive, pouty pose tells me, I can see in my eyes that I know we have a secret.
VO - And Alex wondered how many others had secrets, too.
ALEX BOWLES – ABUSE SURVIVOR

I have found 12 of us in total that are definite victims - 9 don't want to come forward, 3 of us have.
LINK – Back in the seventies, a camera-slinging sweet-talker showered children with compliments and attention by taking questionable photos of them – those children are adults now and they see those photos for what they really are – a reminder of a dark, traumatic past.


VO – In 2018, the Constitutional Court ruled that sexual crimes could be prosecuted regardless of how long ago they occurred opening the door for three adults to demand a price for a childhood tainted by suffering.

Alex, her brother and one other woman stepped forward to demand justice. Last month they filed a fifteen million rand lawsuit against Hardwick.
Suzanne Smith was 11-years old when Hardwick allegedly abused her. But she wasn’t alone either and one day, the children tried to catch him out.
SUZANNE SMITH – ABUSE SURVIVOR

SUZANNE - One of the younger children hid inside the cupboard with a video camera...
VO – So desperate were his young victims, that Suzanne recalls them trying to use Hardwick’s beloved gadgets against him.
SUZANNE SMITH – ABUSE SURVIVOR

SUZANNE - ...so that we could then show it to our parents and say this is what he's doing.

CLAIRE - So what happened that day?

SUZANNE - He clicked that we want to, because it was too many of us in the room.
VO – Our requests for an interview with John Hardwick and his lawyer have gone unanswered.

But last year, Alex got Hardwick's phone number and confronted the now 82-year old.
ALEX BOWLES – ABUSE SURVIVOR

You know you abused me. You know you molested me, and I need you to apologize and he said, well, you know, I don't know if it was that. I might have tickled your legs.
VO - In October, Alex got an email, supposedly from Hardwick.
ALEX BOWLES – ABUSE SURVIVOR

ALEX - The subject line said apologies. For all the harm I have caused, I am so very sorry. I should have contacted you years ago, but I was too scared.

CLAIRE - Did it help at all or not?

ALEX - It did help. The other victims didn't have their chance for that level of closure. It's been a dream of mine to be able to find him, see if he's still alive and confront, so it felt very empowering.
VO – Suzanne received a similar email.
SUZANNE SMITH – ABUSE SURVIVOR

He sends apology letters and then he denies doing it. Why would you apologize for something you say you didn't do?
VO – As they await their day in court, Suzanne says she is stronger but it will be some time before she can truly come to terms with the anger she feels.


SUZANNE SMITH – ABUSE SURVIVOR

CLAIRE - Do you think, after all, is said and done, you'll be able to close this book?

SUZANNE - I hope so. I need to do it for my son, for no one else.

CLAIRE - You are that important for it to be done just for you. You've got this.

SUZANNE – Thank you.

CLAIRE – I've only met you and I'm proud of you. I've only just met you and I'm proud of you


PROMOS

PROMO 1

VO - Poolside parties, family gatherings and the childhood molesters in their midst… Decades later, three women fight for justice against the predators.

PROMO 2

SUZANNE - I remember John always had a camera around his neck

VO - A sweet-talking cameraman, twelve victims and a 40-year old secret – 2 survivors speak out.

ALEX – He's been able to wander through our lives causing destruction.

VO - Now they’re demanding justice.

ALEX - For me, enablers of this sort of crime also have blood on their hands.

PROMO 3

VO - After forty-four years of keeping silent … one woman decided to speak up.

CLAUDINE – My sister and I were abused by two men who had access to us

VO - Years later, there's still no trial date...But she's not giving up...

CLAUDINE – I spent years in therapy. My life did not turn out the way I wanted it to turn out and so I have to be part of this fight back.

metadata.One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...): It took 40 years for these victims to find the courage to expose their abusers and now that they have named and shamed the culprits, the women will stop at nothing to get justice.
metadata.Unique Selling Point: Not only do we speak to Alex and Claudine about their abuse, but we also speak to Suzanne, a victim who has never been interviewed before. We also tell a visually compelling story that incorporates a Cape Talk interview.
metadata.Summary: Victims of an alleged pedophile speak out more that 40 years after the abuse happened. Alex Bowles and her brother John were abused by family friend John Hardwick. Alex talks us through the years of abuse as well as how the adults in their circle, including their parents, enabled it to happen. Alex talks about how her trauma and how that manifested in drug and alcohol addiction as well as eating disorders. She discusses her struggles with nurturing meaningful relationships over the years. She explains the motivation for the R15 million lawsuit against the now 82-year old Hardwick. We also interview Claudine Shiels who also took her abuser to court more than 40 years after the abuse. She took the matter to court in 2017 and will unpack the events of the legal journey in the years that followed, highlighting her wins and losses. Experts provide context for the topic – Zoom interview conducted by Cape Talk with Ian Levit, the lawyer for Alex and an interview with a psychiatrist who discusses grooming behaviour of pedophiles, how enablers create the perfect environment for abuse and how related trauma affects victims.
metadata.Further information: More than anything, in a society where many victims carry the weight of the abuse secret for their whole lives, until they take it to their grave – we put the spotlight on those who have found the courage to speak out and turn to the courts for justice, even after so much time has passed.
